sections.title: Policy and access to the centre
sections.text: Lormont, on the right bank of the Garonne, is mainly shaped by metropolitan rules and a calming scheme at street level. Since 1 January 2025 the low-emission zone applies inside the Bordeaux ring road, 24 hours a day. It bars only vehicles that cannot obtain a Crit'Air sticker, such as petrol or diesel cars registered before 1 January 1997, and those vehicles may still reach 11 listed park-and-rides, including Buttinière and Lauriers in Lormont [0]. The commune set a default 30 km/h limit on almost all its streets from November 2021, keeping only a few main roads at 50 km/h, and says the scheme came with chicanes and parking on the carriageway on some streets, built by the Métropole [16]. A Métropole page announces monthly night-time closures of the Pont d'Aquitaine between the Lormont-Croix Rouge interchange and Labarde, including the night of 21-22 October, Saturday 24 October at 22h and the night of 18-19 November, with traffic diverted by the ring road and the Pont François Mitterrand [17].

sections.title: Parking developments
sections.text: The biggest project is the Buttinière park-and-ride. The commune's project page says the Métropole will extend and renovate the 600-space, four-level car park, which opened in 2004, adding 280 spaces on its east side, with works planned from January 2026 for two years and an estimated 10.8 million euros, and with the car park kept open [9]. A press report of 10 October 2026 gives a later schedule, with the extension built between October 2026 and October 2027, renovation of the old part until summer 2028, 880 spaces in total and 12.2 million euros, which suggests the schedule and the budget changed [10]. The project is to include charging for 176 places, against 8 charging spaces today, but this is a plan [12]. The Métropole's page of 19 May 2026 lists three new park-and-rides (Cadéra, Mermoz, Thouars), the closure of Stalingrad and enlargement of Galin and Buttinière, from text that was first published in 2023 and may be out of date [8]. Metropolis-wide, on-street charging costs 0.38 euro per kWh, with a surcharge of 4 euros an hour after four hours on slow sockets [13]. A press report of 29 September 2026 says the Métropole plans an average 3% rise in TBM fares in 2027, with the park-and-ride ticket going from 4.50 to 5 euros; this is a proposal reported before the council vote [14].

sections.title: Operators, positioning and utilisation
sections.text:
Bordeaux Métropole has a public-service concession with Keolis for its park-and-rides, made official in July 2022, and has put up dynamic signs showing free spaces at five places, including Avenue Carnot in Lormont [7]. The TBM list shows Buttinière with 601 spaces, 16 disabled bays and 8 charging spaces, and Lauriers with 189 spaces, both open to all and linked to tram A [1]. Park-and-rides open only while trams run, with a 15 euro fine for staying outside those hours on one TBM page and 25 euros on another [2]. A ticket costs 4.50 euros, or 3.50 euros at the reduced rate, which applies to Lauriers but not Buttinière, and includes seven round trips that day [3]. The Métropole's own pages give Lauriers 149 spaces against 189 on TBM's list, so the capacities differ [4]. Short stays of two to five days at 12 to 25 euros are sold at Lauriers but not Buttinière [5], and Lauriers is one of six sites in a 300 euro a year overnight offer for residents within 500 m [6]. A press report calls Buttinière the busiest park-and-ride of the metropolis, with about 560 vehicles a day and often full by 8am, and this comes from the press and not from official statistics [11].

Our data cover La Gardette Nord, the park-and-ride that the Métropole places in Lormont and TBM's list places at Avenue des Griffons in Bassens [15], with a feed capacity of 242 spaces, for 27 days since 24 September 2026. Occupancy averaged about 24% on weekdays and 7% at weekends, with a peak of 62% on a Wednesday morning. Buttinière and Lauriers are not in our data.
